Some think the company will be split up and sent to different places as non commissioned officers to drill the National army. Everybody thought we would leave immediately and its sure some disappointment to think we might not go. Can’t tell anything about it though.
I’m on guard duty now. On at 5:30 pm yesterday and off at 5:30 this pm. Do guard duty 2 hours off four hours. It’s pretty cold here at nights but have good warm clothing and a dandy overcoat. I’ll sure be glad to get that sweater. Overcoats are so unhandy to go out to drill but got to wear something to keep warm and that sweater will make it fine and dandy.
I just got away from the guard house for few mins to come over to YMCA and write. Hands are so cold can hardly write.
I’ll be over at club tomorrow night and will write from there.
Be sure and let me know how Knox makes it. Hope rest of you are all well.
In case we leave unexpectedly will write you if permitted.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on September 28, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st Field Battalion
Camp Alfred Vail
Little Silver, N.J.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike County

Camp Alfred, Vail 26th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Golly Havent received any mail since being here. Thought sure would have received a letter before now. Everything going along OK. Awful chilly here but otherwise like it OK. Haven’t heard anything definite as to when we will go to France but were sure going. I’m anxious to get over there. 25 Signal Corps men and 3 officers left today for Franc. 2 come over to the Signal Corps Club nearly every night. Good way to pass time away. Have a dandy Victrola and piano. All kinds books and magazines to read. Been doing lot of fatigue since coming here getting camp straightened out. I haven’t been on a horse since leaving Texas but will go out tomorrow on drill. How are the children coming in school? Is the apple season over yet papa? How much does Grace’s baby weigh now? Lordy I’d love to see her. Did she enter the contest at the state fair? Well guess I’ll go down and finish my story. Am reading “The Dark Star” by Chambers. Have to be back in camp by 11 pm. We all drew overcoats yesterday. The sure are dandy. Will get rest of our winter clothing right away. Fitzjarrellz is over here with me tonight. You know he is the fellow I mentioned from White Hall. Does Ruby remember him? He used to go with Lucille Knox.
Well must stop. Hurry up and write.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Fort Bliss, Texas on August 27, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st F.B.S.C.
Ft. Bliss

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Co “B” 1st FBSC
Ft. Bliss Texas
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa since returning from hike last Saturday evening and sure glad to get them. We went up into New Mexico on the hike. Had a dandy time. The company was split up and strung out through the country and we had continuos wire communication which we put up ourselves. I stayed on duty until midnight. A and C company were along too. A company is the Radio outfit. They put up their wireless apparatus and were in communication with El Paso all the time. They also had a wire strung to our camp and out company relayed all messages for El Paso to the Radio Co and they sent them by wireless to El Paso and Ft. Bliss.
The man who brought Papa’s letter to me yesterday saw that it was from Pearl and asked me if I knew anyone there. I told him I lived there and he said he was from White Hall. He sleeps in tent next to mine. He is a step brother of Pearl Ellis and said he remembered Ruby and Pearl were at their house one time. His name is Fitzjarrellz. He is Corporal in the company and a nice fellow. He also knows Uncle Will’s family at Manchester and used to go with Lucille. Sure surprised me to meet him. Said he had been at Pearl lots of times playing ball and coming to boat shows and knows lots of the fellows around Pearl. He’s the only fellow I’ve ran across close from home. Our battalion played baseball with 2nd telegraph battalion yesterday and beat them 7 to 3. Captain was sure pleased. I had m picture taken in ball suit with another fellow. Just a Kodak. Will send you one soon as they are finished. Mama did you ever find the Kodaks in my suit case?
Well its just 5 min until drill time and I’ve been writing this in an awful hurry so could get it off this am.
Hope everybody is OK. Well write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Fort Bliss, Texas on July 11, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Causal Camp
Ft. Bliss, Texas

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Casual Camp No. 2
Ft. Bliss, TX 7-11
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
No mail since last writing. Expect to be assigned some time this week. I never have received any mail forwarded from Sanderson yet. Should have a good bunch of it pretty soon. Did you get my cards from Juane & Max? Supposed you got my pictures I sent from Sanderson. I’m still doing messenger duty over at Captain’s office. Don’t have much to do. My you ought to see the soldiers drilling here. They get about 3000 out on parade ground and it sure is pretty to see them all moving. They have 6 or 8 bands playing all the time. There’s about 5 camps here at Ft. Bliss. Wouldn’t be surprised if I was assigned to one of them. Quite a bunch of infantry have been sent out of here lately. Some to Eagle Pass, TX, some to Salt Lake City, Utah and some to Syracuse. Wish they would ship me to Illinois. Lordy wish I had come home before enlisting but they told me Tuesday (Day 2 enlisted) that Saturday was last day could volunteer so I thought I’d better get in.
I’ll send my clothes home first time I go to Taylor. Got 2 suit cases full.
Sure hot down here. These uniforms are pretty warm too. Generally go to bed about 8 or 9 pm. Have breakfast at 6 am. Then after breakfast everybody helps clean up camp except men detailed for special duty. They have to pick up every match and scrap on ground and then sweep the entire camp. Some of them have to wait on tables and some work in kitchens about 5 each. I’ve worked both of them. Say I worked in kitchen. I peeled 4 bushel potatoes; scrubbed tables and washed pots. I’ve worked every job they’ve got here expect to clean toilets. We have a dandy shower bath here. Each of us received a Toilet kit yesterday free of charge. Consisting of towel, shaving soap, brush, razor, shoe brush, clothes brush, tooth brush and box shoes polish and a bag to keep them in. Also got package needles and some thread. We’re allowed about 40.00 worth clothes when we enlist. My outfit ran about 15.00. Got 3 suits summer underwear, 3 pair socks, 1 shirt and 1 uniform and pair shoes. Oh yes, got a pair overalls and jacket too. Each of us have our own mess kit consisting of fork, knife, spoon (large), and one pan. We take pan in kitchen and they fill it up. Always have radishes, onions, bread, butter, and ice tea, lemonade, or coffee on table. I’ve never got up from table hungry. We wash our own mess kit and bring them in and put them away. Have a free moving picture show over a 8th calvary every night. We’re free to go where we please from 5>45 pm to 11 pm except Sundays and holidays. We’re off all day except men detailed for special duty, as I am. I did quite a letter writing today. Took bunch papers to Camp Stewart 10 miles distant and then made several other trips on horseback and I’m pretty tired and dusty so I’ll quit and go take bath.
Expect to get a letter from Papa tomorrow for sure.
Sure hope everybody is OK.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed On: July 31, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ills
Pike Co

July 31st
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from papa day before yesterday and one today and mighty glad to get them. General Representative of Russia was here today reviewing our troops. They had a big parade, about 12000 soldiers. Gee it sure looked pretty. As far back as I could see was column after column of soldiers. The signal corps was up toward the front, mounted. I had a pretty good house. By golly from the way paper reads the general had better beat it to Russia. Haven’t heard anything about how long will be here but couldn’t be surprised if didn’t stay here until next spring. It’s pretty warm here in day time but the night are always cool and have to cover up. Thane good thing. Awful glad the girls got their pass to Dunlap. I’ll write to them tonight in this company from Illinois. Sure seems good to see dome one from up there. What is Ralph doing? Hope he gets a job OK. I saw in paper where all the switches around Chad were on a strike. Hope it doesn’t delay the girls trip any.
Well I’m in a hurry. Got to get ready to stand retreat. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Sanderson on June 14, 1917

Sanderson June 13-17
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa today and sure glad to get them. Guess it’s been quite a while since I’ve written. Been feeling pretty glum lately but OK now. It’s blooming hot can’t do anything. I’m sending my resignation in tomorrow and am going to work for Western Union. May come home. I’d like to get away from this hot country, nothing but barren hills. Had big sand storm today but I was in bed and didn’t bother me any. Had my ears full of sand when I got up. Am sending you picture under separate cover. But you were all glad to see Bess, wish I could see you all. Suppose Mama will be home in a few days. Will mail three pictures. Wish you’d give Grace one. Started to mail one to Morrisonville but wasn’t sure she was there. Guess Lucerne will have a good time in Granite. Whats Knox doing anyway? Guess he is doing lots of swimming. I haven’t been swimming since left California.
Well don’t know any news. Everything quiet down here. Wont leave here for week or so yet.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Sanderson on May 31, 1917

Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
I received three letters from papa and one from mama,enclosing Lorin’s and was sure tickled to get them. First mail I had received since leaving Valentine. Sure was too bad about that cyclone. Hope no more of them come along through here. Glad that one didnt hit Pearl. From looks of things I’m going to be here for couple months unless they send a man to relieve me and let me come to El Paso. I got all the clippings Papa sent. Wouldn’t mind being with Pershings expedition if could get a good job. I went over to court house this PM and registered before County Clerk and Mailed it to registrar Pearl, care Sheriff Pittsfield. That way clerk said to address it. I enclosed stamped envelope so he could mail me a receipt. I must be there by the 5th. Should reach there in plenty of time. Golly its sure hot down here. Temperature of 110. Wish I was home. I couldn’t quit very well now if I wanted to account them being so short of operators and couldn’t get relief. This is a very large place. Like it better than Valentine though. It pays 7.50 more on the month. Is Aunt Sarah feeling OK? Hope so. She always was so good to me. Suppose Knox has stumped his toes a dozen times or so. Does he wash his feet before he goes to bed? Hope Lorin gets the job he mentioned. Gee wish I could see that kid of Grace’s. I’ll bet she is some baby. Have any of you been fishing this season yet? I’d like to be there and go squirrel hunting with Papa this season. Golly wish I was home. I only have one dispatcher to work with here. Get along fine with him. I saw him at Del Rio while back. Seems to be a nice man. Sure are a good bunch dispatchers and chiefs at El Paso. They all treat me good there and would show me about different wires and how to adjust a quad.
I worked on a quad most of time I was there. I’d be sending to Houston and Houston would be sending to Opr on other side of me all at same time on same wire. Kinda funny how it works but it does. Four men can work on the same wire, two sending and two receiving. Sure had lots messages. Run about 700 with Houston each day but I didn’t have to do very much. Just about 4 hours steady work with Houston and two hours with Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Well don’t know anything more to write. Sure glad to get that bunch of letters today. Mama hope you write again pretty soon. Papa averages a letter nearly every day and by golly they sure look good.
Hope everybody is well. Hope Vinnie gets well OK.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Langtry, Texas on May 9, 1917

Langtry, Tex 5/9th 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Got her evening of 7th. This sure is some town. One store and 2 or 3 restaurants. Not a very heavy job. Pays $87.50 and commissions all told ought to make it pay 100 but I’ll only be here two or three days longer at least. I can stand on platform and throw across the Rio Grande into Old Mexico. Only about a hundred yards to River. Saw a whole bunch of Mexicans over there yesterday. Don’t know what they were doing. I telegraph from 9 am to 3 pm. Express Commission ran $8.00 last month. Ha. He said it was a very poor month. Don’t have very much to do. Have oil tanks here and have to contend with that but its nothing like Valentine. I kinda wish he hadn’t out me on Valentine agency cause now I’ll have to be running around working relief agencies and can’t stay on my regular job and its more expensive to be running around here and there.
Do hope Margaret is well. Awful glad to hear Lucerne made her grades. How did Knox make it? Too bad Margaret couldn’t take examination. Did I mention receiving Papas and Mamas letters enclosing Bess’? Anyway I did and mighty glad to get them. Haven’t heard anything from Cra yet but expect to in few days. Don’t suppose I could get a pass up there anyway. I got a letter from MK 2 and they said they would be glad to furnish me pass San Antonio to St. Louis provided it was ok with me that they notify this road they had issued such transportation as required by I.C.C. Upon inquiry I found out that if I get pass from MK 2 that the RHASA will blacklist me from their road. They don’t allow their employees to write for their own passes without taking up with them so that knocks me out of pass cause I don’t want to have a bad record here. I don’t see why in the dickens they should care who I get pass from. Guess if they wont furnish transportation I’ll ride the cabooses. Wouldn’t take me very long to get there. Sure will be glad when this war is over.
I’m going to work in Western Union this summer sure. It’s good for $125.00 anytime. They have established an 8 hour day and overtime on Sundays now. That makes W.U. pretty good.
Well must stop and Get busy.
Better write me at Valentine. Expect to be back there by time you get this but if go someplace else can have my mail forwarded.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Valentine on May 3, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Valentine 5/3rd 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Papa’s letter yesterday telling about passage of Conscription law and glad to get it. Guess I’ll stay with the job for a while but I’ll be darned if I wouldn’t like to come home for a while. if I thought there was any chance of having to go to war I’d go join Navy right now cause I’d rather be in navy than in army. Gee they’re sure billing out lots of stock here. Glad I’m off this agency. Got a letter from bess other day. Guess I’ll answer it tonight. Have plenty of time on this job now. Business pretty light.
Gee it’s warm here at night now. They say mosquitoes are awful bad here in summer. Golly I’ll be it gets awful hot here in summer.
How’s Coa fixed for operations now? Wouldn’t mind having a relay job up there.
Maybe I’ll write J.L.M. for a job. I don’t like this County a bit. It’s too windy.
Well I don’t know a thing to write so will stop. Hope everybody is OK.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Eliojah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: El Paso, Texas on June 10, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

St. Blanca
January 10, 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all;
Received 2 letters from Papa today. One via valentine and I was glad to get them both. Didn’t think you’d be able to get one to St. Blanca so quick. Nothing new to write. Getting along O.K. I called up both last night and asked them what they wanted me to do in case one called while I was working with other and they said just use my own judgement and if I pay no attention to them they get sore. I’m hitting the ball here pretty lively. Keep busy every minute of the night. The depo I trick open copied a 19 for a IP 2/5 train this pm to meet another IP No. 2 train at Fort Hancock. No. 2 got to Fort Hancock and waited 2 hours for the 2nd 5 to show up but they didn’t so he called up Dispr. on phone and went on. 2nd No. 5 was in a blind siding down the line. They claimed they didn’t get the order. Disp. came after open about it and open looked for his clearance and he had it non clearance so it will be up to the train creed.
Well, must stop. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: England on January 9, 1917

Somewhere in England
Jan 9th
Dearest Folks,
Thought I’d write few lines tonight while have time but can’t tell you much except that I’m feeling OK and had a pleasant voyage.
It’s pretty cold here but not any worse than New Jersey.
Am not allowed to mention hardly anything so don’ expect to learn anything about the war from me.
Rode on an English train other night. They’re a great deal different from ours. They are built in compartments. Each compartment sealing 8 men (3rd class). No way of getting from one compartment to another except by getting off and entering another. Just like traveling in a carriage.
Had a good stateroom on the steamer and didn’t get a bit seasick.
I’ll write you again in few days and don’t worry if you don’t hear from me regularly. Hope you are all well-
Lots Love
Martin
Address Exactly Like This:
Martin W. Chandler
Co B 126 Field Bin Dig Corps
American Exp Forces

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Sierra Blanca January 2, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Sierra Blanca Jan 2, 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Got in here last night and went to work. Job is enough to keep a man busy but not so awful hard. Have a night helper to handle baggage, etc. So I don’t have to do anything but telegraphy and clear trains on Both TP na dishes. I’m plumb disgusted with board here. This place is about the size of Hillview and only one place in town to board and they sure treat a fellow awful. Have to carry wash hater to your room and no carpet and just about the poorest accommodations a man could find. Got 1 pork chap, 2 biscuits and a few friend potatoes for breakfast and thats all. I got up from the table hungry. Charge 30.00 month. I went to bed right after breakfast this morning and got up at exactly 10 minutes after seven and they told me I was too late for supper. Had to go buy a meal at Brown’s News. They know they have a fellow cinched and they don’t care how they treat them. I asked how much for just a room and they said just the same as for board and room. Now what do you think of that? I was figuring on getting my meals at restaurant but they queered that. It’s just plain hold up. They know you can’t get any place else to stay.
If I stay here I’m sure going to get the Co to give me a box car or else build some kind of shanty and go to Baching. Can’t possibly get by for less than 35 to 40 a month for board the way it is now. If I get up after supper time I have to buy a meal and its hard to arrange sleep so can get breakfast and supper both cause I generally sleep 10 hours. Here I never eat more than 2 meals a day and they wont give me one of those if I happen to be late but they charge for it. Just the same – I told the manager what I thought abut it and he informed me I had the privilege of going some place else to board if I didn’t like it, which of course he knew I couldn’t get any place else. I’m going to every house intern tomorrow and see if I can’t get a room.
Job pays 85 don’t get the 5.00 for handling mail as the night helper does that.
Have lots trains to clear. Just twice as many as at Valentine cause here we get the Tp. trains too but don’t mind it as long as don’t have to handle baggage and mail.
Pretty cool here. They say they have cold winters here.
Well its now 11:45 s will stop and get things lined up to go to work. Work from 12 to 8.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Grace Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Grace Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Sent From: Morrisonville on October 1, 1916

Morrisonville 10/1/16
Dearest Papa, Mama, & all: –
Guess you think it’s about time I was writing – Bess and I just got back from Sunday School. We took a spurt this am and got ready and went to the Presbyterian SS and everyone treated us so nice we are glad we went. bess is correcting some papers and making out some examination papers and I have dinner on cooking. Did think I would come in and play the graphonolia but thot I would be making better use of my time if I write home.
Ruby left yesterday morning and we sure miss her. Bess and i took her to the train, had to get up at 6 am so we could have breakfast and get to the depot by 6:58 am.
Bess and i then came home, cleaned the house real good and she had to go to a teachers reading circle at 2 pm. I dusted and scrubbed after she left took a bath and dressed up again and went to meet her. Got there in time to hear part of the work. We walked up town again went to Callie’s and she insisted on us staying and having supper. So Lorin came in on the 6:30 pm train and we went to meet him and all took supper there. Then went to the picture show. Lorin bought me the most beautiful purple velvet tricornered hat for my birthday, he said, but that isn’t until the 6th of next month. So he was in plenty of time – Ha. My white coat just got back this am from the cleaners, so you make know I wore my new hat and white coat to S.S. and felt quite dressed up. Bess cleaned her lack suit yesterday and wore my other purple hat.
Our electric washer came yesterday pm and Lorin got up early this morning and had it in working order by the time we got up. It sure us a peach and I’m tickled we have it – will sure save my back.
Lorin is going to Taylorville to get out car today, had to leave it up there the last time he was up there, on account of some man running into him and busting it up some. Will cost about $30 to get it fixed up again. Lorin sued him for $200 – the trail comes up next week. Hope he gets what it will cost us. The car is alright now so he is going to get it today.
I am cooking apples whole not peeled, with such red skin, also sweet potatoes, kraut pork & wieners. Have raw tomatoes with mayonnaise dressing for dinner.
How is papa? You said he was not feeling well when you last wrote. Hope is better by now. Guess Margaret & Lucerne will have a great time in St. Louis. Lorin said I could go, but I don’t believe I want to. It would be different if he and Bess could both go.
I was surprised Leta & John stayed in Pearl to spend their honeymoon. Guess they have gone to St. Louis by now.
Mon. P.M. Guess I’ll finish this and get it mailed. After dinner yesterday we drove to Taylorville with Oren Bloxom and another fellow, attended a football game, and drove our own car back home. Oren Bloxom came back with us – He’s a Taylorville boy, and is going to be a lawyer. Bess entertained him until his train time. I was so tired, Lorin and I went to bed. I had lunch for all.
Lorin forwarded two letters to Ruby this a.m. I told him to send them to Pearl I was afraid she wouldn’t get them if we sent them to Granite City.
I pulled the pears, Ruby will be glad to know and have just finished two gallons of pear butter. I had them on hand for over two weeks, so you may be sure I’m glad they’re cooked up.
Lorin is going to put up the base burner this afternoon. It isn’t very cold yet but he thought he’d better put it up while he had time.
Bess said at noon that she must write home. I told her I had a letter started.
She has four sets of papers to correct this evening after she comes home. She’ll be pretty busy this week with giving examinations and correcting papers.
I wish papa could come up if only for a few days, might do him good and we would be tickled to death to have him. Some of you could get a pass and come up anytime. Well this is all I can think of for now. Lorin will be down around that part of the country next week, I suppose.
Write when you can, we’re always ticked to hear from home.
Much love to all,
Lovingly,
Grace
Tues. A.M. –
Am sure going to get this mailed this morning. We have a train out of here for St. Louis at 3:37 P.M. and Lorin was just saying at the breakfast table that we could go down and see the Veiled Prophet tonight and get home on the midnight train if Bess could get her Supt. to teach for her half hour. So no telling we may be there tonight ourselves. The matter is to be settled at noon after Bess talks with the Supt. and Lorin is to study it over.
Write soon.
Grace

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 20, 1916

M.W. Chandler
Southern Pacific Company
Santa Margarita, Cal.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co.

Santa Margarita, Spet. 20
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Received a letter from Papa yesterday and a long on today and was sure glad to get them. Gee they sure are doing some business back there. Think I told you in other letter I’d be here a month longer and possibly two. Glad to hear Ralph is back at work. I don’t want to work on era very bad but I’d like awful well to be closer to home. Gee I wish I could see some of you . I sold a ticket to Waterburg Conn last night – $72.40- I didn’t have any ticket on hand so I wired Sam Luis Abirro to send me one and gave him the routing and he sent it up all made out. Excursion tickets are on sale the year round. Every Friday and Saturday have reduced rates to nearly all the places along the line. Can get a ticket to Chicago and return for $65.00.
Sure have some powerful engines on this line. They’re all oil burners. Haven’t a coal burner on the line.
I stuck a first class passenger train 5 minutes yesterday morning account putting “9th” for “September” – They might give me 10 days for it – They’re awful strict. They all say that if you can work for the S.P. you can work for any road in the country. They sure enforce their rules. I was in a hurry to make out the clearance as train was ready to leave and without thinking I put 9/20 instead of September 20 – That’s OK on any other road but this one. It takes about 3 years to land a job on this road. But if extra work is good I think I’ll stick. Of course I’d probably lay off and come home before 3 years. But these are pretty good jobs and I want to land something steady if I can. I don’t have to fill lamps or lanterns or sweep out or handle baggage or anything like that. Have a baggage boy to do that. All stations have a baggage boy. All I have to do is sell tickets, copy orders, and put on mail. Sure copy a bunch of orders and seek quite a few tickets.
Well must stop. Hope to hear from you all soon-
I’ll write more often
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 18, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike Co

Santa Margarita Sept 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Mama’s letter yesterday and haven’t heard from papa in a coons age. Sure was glad to get Mama’s letter. This is first time I’ve written for several days. Getting along OK and will be on this job at least a month longer and probably 2 months. Agent has gone to New York so regular 3rd trick man got his job leaving me here for while longer. Sure have a bunch of train orders to handle. Keeps me going sometimes. Getting pretty cool out there at night. Have to have a fire every night. See in the paper where they have rented the M.E. Church for Primary room. Thought they had built a new school house there or had added to the old one. See they’ve started on the ditch again. I’d like to see it.
I’ve been going up to the school-man’s house nearly every night. We all went swimming other day. Gee they have swell schoolhouse here. Have piano, dance floor, opera house, and everything in it. Have some pretty swell scenery on the stage. It’s a single story building but has 4 rooms besides the opera and dance room. Sure is swell.
Gee I sure was tickled when agent told me he was going to lay off 2 months. Felt pretty sure I’d get to stay on this job. Ruby is making a pretty good visit at Grace’s. Wish I was there.
Well I must stop and get busy. Bell rings just about every 10 or 15 min for 9.00. Wish you’d all write a little more often.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on August 9, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Santa Margarita 8/9 1916
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from Papa yesterday and sure glad to get it. Nothing new to write. Getting along OK. It has been pretty cool here last 2 days. Had to build fire last night and got one going tonight. All the people around here treat me just fine.
Mama I haven’t received the pictures yet. Will enclose stamps to send them. Would like to have the Tribune occasionally too. I’m going to to subscribe for it pretty coon. Was intending to go swimming today but it was too cold. Played ball with Santa Margarita last Sunday and guess will play again next Sunday.
I’m feeling pretty bum today. Caught a bad cold but guess I’ll be ok in day or two. Well must stop as don’t know anything to write. Everybody write soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: June 3, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

June 3rd, 1916
Dearest Folks
Just left Seattle at 1 pm on S.S. “Tacoma.” Now on Pacific Ocean bound for Portland, ore. Sure great think maybe will go to work in Portland. Don’t know for sure yet whether can get on or not. Keep on writing me at Frisco. Received long letter from Grace in Seattle.
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Ellensburg, Washingto on June 2, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

Ellensburg, Wash. June 2, 1916
Dearest Folks,
Just came in this am. Leaving this pm for Seattle. This sure is pretty little town. So many trees. Be sure and write me at San Francisco.
MC

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Denison, Texas on February 19, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike Co.

Denison, Tex. 2/18
Dearest Folks,
Arrived there last night and went to work this am. Been all day checking the place up. Had over 1000.00 worth commisionary goods. Sure am tired tonight. Got a letter from Sam yesterday – said you were worrying cause I hadn’t been writing. Having sweep weather another month with bring the summer.
Sure got a lot of work ahead of me to get straightened out. Guess I’ll be OK in couple days though.
This job pays $30.00 and board. If I stay here this summer will be getting 40 by then.
Only have 30 men in this gang. I have to keep track of their meals and purchases and charge them for it. Sales amounted to 18.00 yesterday. Will get my first pay the 15th of March. Have about $12.00 coming. Sure going to try and save a little if I can. May stay with this job for quite awhile and again may not. Tell better when summer comes.
Well will close-feel awful sleepy.
Sure like to hear from all of you often.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Denison, Texas on February 7, 1916

Mr. E. H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

M. Chandler
K18 Denison, Tex

Denison, Feb 5
Dearest Folks,
Gee wish I hadn’t told you not to write sure miss the mail. Expected to get out by first of month but account of work closing down on Union Pacific all the men came down here so I may be here a week yet. want you all to write me right away. Am enclosing letter from Ft. Worth so you see I can’t tell exactly when I will get out. Having pretty good time. Gained 12 pounds since being down here and feel fine. Sure have good meals.
I put out pretty good washing today. Washed bed clothes beside my clothes. Last 5 days sure have been swell. Couldn’t ask for better weather. I’m 5 miles out from Denison now but still get mail at Denison-K-18-
You just keep on writing and if I leave I can have it forwarded. Hope everybody is well. Is Ruth still there?
Well I don’t know hardly anything to write so will close.
Hope to hear from all of you soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Hillsboro, Texas on January 14, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Hillsboro, Tex Jan 14, 1916
Dearest Folks,
Thought I’d write few lines this am. I’ve been going on so much about how warm it was and night before last it dropped to 10 degrees about zero. I was in a box car all night and it was certainly cold. I didn’t go to Greenville with Mr. Coster as expected. Stayed in San Antonio another day trying to get a job. I came to Hillsboro and have been treated fine. The above company have their bunk cars here and they have me my meals and the foreman gave me a splendid letter to W.L. Hilt to help me towards getting a job. Says it don’t pay very much to start but good chance for promotion for right man. Sure have reacted me like a prince. I’ll go from here to Dallas and then to Greenville to get my clothes and then to Ft. Worth to see this company. Ft. Worth is close to Dallas but will have to go to Greenville to get my clothes account can’t have them forwarded. With the letter I have, I certainly ought to be able to get something. Will send you a copy of the letter. It is about 20 degrees above zero this am and am sure glad I’ve a good warm place to stay while I’m here.
This Mr. Allen who gave me the letter hadn’t know me but about 5 hours when he gave it to me. Sure is a nice man.
Well I’ll write you soon as get to Ft. Worth and see what I can get. Hope everything is well and OK.
Lovingly,
Mart

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: San Antonio, Texas on January 6, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

San Antonio, Jan 6
Dearest Folks,
Just wrote this am but have changed my mind and will leave for El Paso, TX tonight. Could find nothing here. Will try and write a letter soon. Write me at El Paso, Tex. Will have mail forwarded from here.
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: New Orleans, LA on December 25, 1915

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ills
Pike County

New Orleans Dec 25th
Dearest Folks,
Sure don’t seem like Christmas. Leave here this pm. Probably be in Houston Tuesday or Wednesday unless land something before I get there. Lots of great sights here. Went through Louisiana State Museum yesterday evening. Sure interesting. Was also down to Wharves where they were unloading cargo of bananas. Will write again soon.
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: New Orleans, Louisiana on December 24, 1915

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co

New Orleans, La Dec 24
Dearest Folks,
Nothing going yet. Going stay over until tomorrow and then to Houston. Sure be glad to hear from you. Swell weather. Hope to land something either here or in Houston. Write from Houston. Merry Xmas and Happy New Year.
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Cleveland, Mississippi

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Cleveland Miss Dec 21
Dearest Folks,
No job yet. Leaving tonight, be in New Orleans about Wednesday or Thursday. Kinda slow traveling. Be sure and write me at Houston, Tex. Hope everybody is well. Regular summer days here will write from New Orleans.
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Robinsonville, Mississippi on December 20, 1915

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Robinsonville, Miss 20
Dear Folks,
Just for here this am. Pretty warm. Probably be in New Orleans Tuesday or Wednesday and then to Houston, Tex if don’t land anything in New Orleans. Wish you would write to me at Houston, Tex.
-Martin

item.title: From: Lorin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Lorin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Patono, Kansas on June 21, 1919

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Patono, Kan 6/21/19
Dear Folks,
On our way to Wichita. Left McLune at 8:40 both feeling fine, will write later.
Love,
Lorin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: San Antonio, Texas on January 6, 1915

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

San Antonio, Jan 6
Dearest Folks,
Received mama’s letter this am forwarded from Houston and say I sure was glad to get it. I’ve been up to Del Son Pac Dispr. twice but nothing doing. Going to MKJ and LGM today too. Write me here.
Lovingly,
Martin
Getting along OK. Feel good.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: San Antonio, Texas on January 5, 1915

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

San Antonio Tex Jan 5
Dearest Folks,
Just arrived here this am. Pretty nice town. Haven’t found anything yet. Will probably stay here 3 or 4 days and get my mail. If I do leave can have it forwarded . Sure is warm here. More so than in Houston. I’ll probably go from here to Ft. Worth. Sure wish I had a job. Hope everybody is OK. Would like to be there but no chance. Ha. Will let you know for sure in day or 2 where am going.
Martin

item.title: From: Ruby Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Ruby Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Wichita, Kansas on October 23, 1912

Wichita, Kansas October 23, ’12
Dearest Papa, Mamma, and All:
We received the children’s and Papa’s letters yesterday, Mamma’s registered and Bess’ letters today so I feel especially good tonight.
I was awfully glad to get the $15.00 for Martin’s suit. Will order it Saturday, then he’ll get it in a week. After this month thought I will have gotten a good start and wont be so hard pressed for extra coin. We’ll get a pay day a few days earlier this month on account of the Topeka trip. Say Papa I wish you’d order it right away for Ill need it the 6th and thats a short time off. order it Via Rock Island as a special is chartered for the benefit of Wichita teachers and promises to get us there in about 14 and a half hours.
I was glad Bess sent that music. I have those two you mentioned but can’t locate the song book. Will tell you later what I do and what happens.
Bess, I was rather depending on you ordering my hat thru Edna, since you were going to pay me a little on my coat than $5.00. But if you can’t share it, I can wait until I get my next pay and get it here the day before I go to Topeka for I can’t get it right now.
Form the way your letters read it seemed you didn’t get my last one for in it I asked about my hat and told you what I wanted also told Mamma on back of envelope it was ok about bed trade.
If you can’t order hat thru Edna I’ll first get a sailor for I’d have to pay a sum for beaver and trim it like I want it. Ethyl and I rented a piano and it was moved in last Sat. so I feel so much more at home. I was first crazy about before I got it. I sure will put in the time. Martin learned to play “Rock of Ages” clear thru with both hands. He’s awfully proud of it. ha! He’s onto Mae’s now. I had to go to Teacher’s Association and a dinner afterwards so he went out there. I had him go to a “Delicatessen” right near us, for his supper and go out there afterwards. I haven’t seen her since Sunday but called her up this noon and she said she’d be down after school tomorrow. I did quite a washing last night and ironed this a.m. before I went to school so as to be ready for that down tonight. I wore my white veil and a tight red low made from the ribbon on my summer hat, put it right in the back. It looked good. I had several compliments. You know, my veil dress split in 3 or 4 places and I took it to Boston Store and showed them and they gave me $2.50 due bill for material. So I got a wide insertion and set it in which also lengthened it just enough. I’m quite proud of my handiwork. I still have $1.00 of that left. Not in money but due – bill. It will come in handy sometime.
I am going to a show this week and wear my light blue dress. Ethyl had a fit over it. I agent been ad it on yet. I will be the first show I have seen, not even the princess. Sam is join got take me to Forum Friday night.
I’m glad Grace got her a traveling bag. One needs it so often. Mine will come in handy at Topeka. Say, I fixed my blue dress up dandy so I can wear it all winter. I cleaned it and pressed it and put the waist back on so it looks most as good as new. I’ll clean my lavender so I can take both to the convention.
Say, I have got a peachy coat. It’s a mixture and has big lapels of broadcloth. It’s as swell as any I’ve seen. It’s the bicle cloth, pretty rough mostly black, so a black hat will go well with it. Bess did you get your grey beaver trimmed with pink. I saw one down town, and it would be so pretty for you.
Grace are you wearing your suit or your cast winter coat? You didn’t mention so I wondered. Your blue suit was pretty on you.
The children’s letters were so cute. I can read them over and over and laugh every time. It sure tickles Martin to hear what Knox says. He says “Don’t you wish we had him here.” I have thought so often how much good it would do one of the little girls here with we while they were out of school so long. I want them to have music so bad. After awhile I’m going to ave Martin play. He wants to so bad and it seems easy for him.
I forgot to tell you how I paid for my coat. Why since I’m a teacher I can run a bill, so whatever is absolutely necessary I can get there anytime. It came in handy for I needed it so bad when I got my dresses, I still wear my suit lots but its so hard to keep my waist ironed. I had them rough dried at the Steam Laundry also sheets, pillow cases and table cloths and Martin’s collars, came to $0.47. I’m going to have them laundered every 2 weeks, then do my own ironing. It’s sure worth that much and more to have them clean.
I have some of the cutest pictures Mae and I made. Cut out magazine pictures and pasted them on gown mats. Some are of Sat. evening pasts. Adds lots to my room.
I made some dandy corn fritters for supper last night and had some left for dinner today. It’s so handy having some thing already fixed for quick brunch at work. The mail usually comes at noon and I have a time popping from stove to letters getting them read.
I’ll sure take time to write Aunt Sarah later also to Pearl. Girls I’ve had several cards from Irvin Pounds with his address – gentle hint! Guess I’ll write him too.
You’ve asked so many time about color of Martin’s suit and I forget to answer. He wants brown mixture and its very popular too. A sort of red brown then he wants brown shoes before he comes home so of course I’ll be able to get them then. He takes real good care of his appearance – as good as possible. He can spend a good deal time at Mae’s or over to Sam’s (he usually does) while I am at Topeka and sorts rough about for his meals down here. I feel safe enough about leaving him so much with Sam. They’re pretty good roomies. And he likes Mrs. D.D. too she jollies with him so much. Don’t mention anything about being afraid to leave him in your letters but you might tell him to make the best of everything while I’m away. I know where he is every minute for he gets out a certain time and I know he doesn’t waste much getting here. he looks fine and never coughs one, since he had that cold.
Grace, it’s about time you were writing again. I’d like to write lots more but will have to go to bed its 11:20 and I was up late last night. Guess I’ll write on the other side tho. Say Mrs. Mussenbach must want her fame as a poctiss to spread abroad. I saw two in the paper last week. Guess I’ll send Carrie a card, and put my address on it. Hers is just Woodriver but I’ll put c/o Washington School, Cleveland Ave.
I’m rather anxious to know the outcome of the settlement, so is Mae. Art asked Mae what she was going to do with her half. He’s pretty busy making Xmas presents. Guess he don’t want the worry of it right at the last. Must close. Write as often as you can. It’s a deal to look forward to after school hours to expect mail. I think thats why Martin rushes home so.
Love to All,
Ruby

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family

Mailing Address:
Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Return Address:
M. Chandler
COB 1st BSC
Mammouth Parking

9 am Indianapolis, Mo. 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, & all
En route to Mammouth Park, Mo. Cmae through K.C. & St. Louis both but was only in each place 15 minutes and was way down in yards. We weren’t allowed to leave train at all. Just now pulling into Maple. Intended to write you from KC but no chance. We came through St. Louis at 11 pm last night. Rock bends El Paso to St. Louis and then St. Louis to destination. Should reach New Jersey about night. All the trains are taking siding for us and we have had a clear track since leaving Mt. Bliss. Delayed occasional by broken tunnel on one of the car horses and then we have to unload them every 3 hours and let them rest 8 hours. All the little towns in Missouri and Kansas had word of our coming and school was dismissed and they were all down to station with flags to wave at use. One girl passed out a basket of cigarettes. from way they are rushing us am inclined to think we will go on over to France although some say we are going to camp in NJ for winter. We have dandy pullman and good meals. Having fine trip. Didn’t come through Wichita. Wanted to bad too. Came through Hutchinson, Kans. Well I’m in hurry so can mail this here in Maples cause don’t know when we will stop again. Will write you just as soon as get to New Jersey and give you my address.
Love to all
Martin
(over)
P.S.
Suppose you get the Battalion picture my picture isn’t a bit good. Can hardly be recognized. Am in the sixth grow from the right and third row right next to the big black horse on cart.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: McNary, LA. on December 29

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co.

Dearest Folks,
Was out of post cards and couldn’t write. This is first place I’ve stopped off since leaving New Orleans. Will be in Houston Friday. Sure am anxious to get there so can get my mail. Would liked to have sent something to you all for Xmas but couldn’t. Railroads down here pay pretty good wages but plenty of men will be leaving here pretty soon. This is just small place. Have saw mill here.
Am enclosing a handkerchief for Mama. Wish I could have sent something better for your birthday. Will write again soon. Sure would like to get a job. Hope you are all well.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Cairo, Ill. on December 16

Cairo, Ill. Dec 16
Dearest Folks,
Getting along OK. Leave here today. Sure hope I can get a job. it’s pretty cold down here but don’t mind it much. Rather be traveling this way than to be laying round in Pearl. Sure would like to hear from yours. I can imagine what you all think of me for leaving this way especially while Grace and Lorin were there but think I’d rather be most anywhere than Pearl.
Next time I write I’ll give you an address and want to hear from some of you.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey October 18

Oct 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received papas letter yesterday and Bess’ dandy letter today and mighty glad to get them. I came over other night and wrote but forgot to mail it so guess it has been quite a while since you’ve heard from me. The 11th Reserve battalion left for France this morning. We got our lockers back this am also got stoves so guess we will camp here this winter from looks of things but of course can’t tell for sure. I think they intended to send one battalion over and hadn’t decided who to send hence our preparedness but now since the 11th have gone we’re likely to stay here for some time. I’ve been getting the Pike Country Republican lately. Who’s sending it? It has news from boys at Camp Taylor. Saw Wade’s and Jesse’s picture in it.
Tell Parish I’ll write the Tribune a letter relative Army Life as far as I knew. Don’t know anything about it except Signal Corps Branch. Awful glad to hear Knox’s arm is healing. Hope he doesn’t fall from some place and break it again before it mends. We’ve been out on target range 3 days out of this week and go again tomorrow. I can shoot pretty well. Scored 76 out of 100 first time. I even tho one of the automatic pistols. Lots pretty good shots in this company. Is Aunt Sarah still at our house?
They are offering liberty bonds to our company on installment plans. We have about 75 men and they’re taken $4200.00 so far. I can’t take any account the allotment home. Have o pay at rates $10.00 per month and thats all I’m getting. By the way, you’ll get first payment 1st of December. Captain said it was paid one month behind June all the time and then you’ll get the last one a month after I’m out of army. Gee Margaret is getting rather popular. Having bunch of fellows wanting to call on her.
It’s pretty chilly here. heavy frosts each morning. Well I’ll stop now and go back to camp. Pretty tired tonight. On our feet all day today fixing stoves for the company. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on July 22

Santa Margarita
July 22nd
Dearest Papa and All,
Just received letters from you, mama, Lucerne and Margaret fe minutes ago and was sure glad to get the. Wish they would come that way all the time. I wrote yo Mama few minutes ago and wrote to her day before yesterday in Morrisonville so guess she will get it soon after she gets there.
Getting along OK on the job. Coping about 50 train orders last night and had 43 Expense Bills. Handle mail or 3 trains and sell tickets for 3 trains so there’s generally enough to keep me busy. Like the job fine though. Theres lots of fellows here wanting to lay off and can’t get relief. M en are awful scarce but in the winter time they close so many offices that it throws a whole bunch of men on extra board but extra work looks pretty good for this winter and if I earn to handle an agency by that time will be assured of almost steady work. These agencies pay big money too. Do you and Knox get any fish? That was a pretty good string you caught the other day. Bet Knox was tickled to yank them out.
Wish I was there so could go squirrel hunting few times. Gee the girls sure are bathing lots berries. Hope Ruby is feeling better. Golly I haven’t heard a piano for so long I’ve forgotten how one sounds. Hope Ralph will be able to go back to work soon. Too bad Micky had to take sick.
Well the train is coming now that I want to get this off on so will close. Wish all of you would write. Hope everyone is OK. Will send Annie a card right away.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on March 10

France Mar 10th
Dearest Folks,
Will write just few lines tonight while have good chance. Nothing new to write. Have received no mail yet. Suppose it will be several months before you can get a letter to me at this address. Requires quite a while to get an answer to a letter.
Have moved since last writing. Would like to tell you of our locations. Things are pretty warm here.
Been having some very nice weather here for past week. Hope it continues.
I’ve been feeling very good. Get plenty to eat. Have a pretty good YMCA here. Affords a good place to write letters.
Well must close and turn in. Am on K.P. now and have to get up at 4 am.
Hope you are all feeling well.
Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
P.S. Dont have any of my letters put in “Tribune.”

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on February 28

Dearest Folks,
Have been traveling about quite a bit since last writing you. Was transferred to the 117th F.B.S.C. Feb 12. Like the organization very well and if I had my mail, clothes, etc from the 1st FB would just as soon stay with this organization. My service record is still with my old company. Don’t know when I’ll get a pay. Haven’t received any pay since October. Would like very much to get the mail you’ve already sent to me at 1st FB. But don’t know whether or not it will be forwarded here.
Been having some very rainy weather the past week. Guess this is the rainy season. First I’ve seen since being over here.
Would like to tell you of our whereabouts but of course that’s forbidden.
Am feeling very good. Only hope you are all feeling as well. Must stop for this time. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
Address: Pvt. Martin W. Chandler
Co ‘C” 117 F.B.D.C.
A.E.F.
Via New York

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, California

M.W. Chandler
Santa Margarita, Cal
8034 Santa Margarita

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Dearest Papa, Mama, and All
Received letter from Papa yesterday and sure glad to get it. I’ve been working 2nd trick for last 2 days. 2nd trick man laid off and man they sent to relieve him couldn’t handle 2nd account so much clerical work to do. Don’t think he can handle 3rd either. Agent wired them that he was putting me on 2nd. Gee I have lots of clerical work to do. Have at least 10 car loads of wood, ore, and apples, each day. Ore all goes to Niagara Falls. Costs $750.00 per car to ship it. Have both Ford and Reed abstracts to make out, damage reports, write up freight bulls in cash book, have to make out Western Union and Tuckit report at end of month. Work from 4 pm to 12 but generally come to work at noon. Came over at noon today and made out ticket report and Western Union up to date. So wouldn’t have so much to do tomorrow. I’ll be on this job for about a week longer and when regular 2nd tick man comes back agent said he would see that I got the 3rd trick back. He came over to hotel and awakened me and asked if I would work 2nd trick. I like the job OK. Get lots of good sleep now. I have 3 passenger trains to sell tickets for and both locals and 2 regular freight trains on this trick but don’t have to get outside of office. Local conductors unload freight and wheel it in warehouse and seal cars and baggage boy handle the passenger trains and check baggage. All I have to do is make out switch lists and clear them. Have quite a few orders but not as many on 3rd trick. Both locals get along between 10 and 11 pm.
Only thing I don’t like about this job is having to work evenings. I’ve been going up to see a bunch of school teachers every night and have lots of fun. Two of them are Catholic and I get into some awful arguments with them some times. All nice girls though. Always have some candy made or a bunch of fruit. Have a swell Victrola and two of them play the piano.
How’s Knox getting along in school? Is Uncle Jim any better? Hope Aunt Sarah is ok.
Well must stop and get busy. Hope you all write soon. Lucerne I haven’t heard from you for a long while. Guess Hipockets is waiting till he learns to spell before he writes. Ha. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on January 27

France Jan 27
Dearest Folks,
Intended writing yesterday but out it off until today.
Will leave hospital tomorrow but probably wont join my company for a month. Will go from here to convalescent camp and will be there 2 weeks and then go to base where will remain while longer so guess I wont get any mail for some time yet as all my mail will be with company. I haven’t had any pay for 2 months. Guess wont get any until I join company. I’m dead broke too but guess wont have much use for money for while anyway. I’ll have about 40.00 when

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Ahrweiler, Germany on January 26

Ahrweiler, Germany
Jan 26
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from Papa day before yesterday dated Jan. 1st and very glad to get it and to know everybody is well. Was very anxious to know that Mama and Anna had recovered from the attack of influenza. Think I mentioned in a previous letter that I had received a bunch of my back mail including letters from Ruby, Grace, and Lorin.
Not very much news to write. Persistent rumors indicate that we will leave next month. Most of the rumors sound very plausible and I’m beginning to put a little faith in them. Certainly would love to get home. I’m still on the same job. Business has been rather heavy last few days. Was notified few days ago that I would attend Liaison School at Coblens but have heard nothing definite about it since so don’t know whether or not I’ll go. Hope so anyway.
The people here are as cordial as ever. They don’t seem to be suffering in the least. All the families I’ve seen so far have had plenty of food. I ate supper with a German family (Place where I room) other night and they had roast pork, something I hadn’t tasted for a year.
Has been pretty cold last few days. Has snowed several times lately but not heavily.
Having quite a bit of entertainment through the Red Cross, K of C and YMCA shoes have been pretty good. The 2nd Canadian Division met the 42nd (Rainbow) Division in an athletic contest short time ago. We won the meet by quite a margin. I attended the boxing bouts. We won 5 out of the 6 matches, scoring two knockouts. Had a very large attendance.
Well must close for this time. Want to write to Grace tonight. Wrote to girls at Wichita several days ago.
Hope this finds you all well. I’m feeling fine and dandy. Write often.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Del Rio, Texas on January 8

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co

Del Rio Tex Jan 8
Dearest Folks,
Still moving. Just got here this am. Going to Eagle puss tonight and down into Old Mexico. Am only mile and half from line. Will write soon. Probably be in El Paso about next Wed or Thursday.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey

Mr. E. H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

5th
Dearest papa mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa day before yesterday. Awful glad to get them. Was just starting home from club and thought would drop you couple lines right quick. Nothing new to write. Don’t know when we will leave. Nobody seems to know. May be here until Christmas and again may leave within the week. We’re all prepared to leave immediately. They fixed up the allotment for me today.
You will get 20.00 about 1st of Nov. and each month from then on for 1 year. I wont have 20 myself to send it home now. Seems like it slips through my fingers just as I get it. Hope everybody is well. Am in hurry just now so will stop and write more some other time.
Feeling fine.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Bess Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Bess Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family

Sunday
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Sure do thank you for then five. Came in handy but I want you to know I earned the money to pay for my Xmas presents. Got $22 for my first case of nursing. No I didn’t either, Mae gave me $10.00 for staying with her. I didn’t want to take that but she just insisted and as I was altogether broke it looked awfully good. Then at Temps I stayed one week and 3 days for $22. Didn’t have anything to do but take care of the little girl. They treated me fine and invited me to stay over Xmas with them and eat turkey dinner but I wanted to eat with the girls. When I left the little girl I was nursing gave me an Xmas present. The sweetest little apron with tattling all around the the pieces set together with tatting wasn’t that nice? I have another place now out on College Hill. Three people down and I’ll get $30.00 a week here. I gave M & L $5.00 between them after Xmas. Lucerne is going to get her a pair of shoes. Margaret got hers and I got mine. They are awfully good looking.
Our Xmas we sent home looked kind of slim didn’t it? I just had one day to shop and I had to wait until I made some money to shop with. I was picking out Xmas cards and found one like the one we sent home. I thought it had lots of good thoughts and it also there was a lot of loving thoughts with out gifts. Grace sent me a pair of silk stockings and Mae gave me a pair too. Mrs. D.D. gave each M, L, and I a drop de china handkerchief. They surely treated Ruby and Sam as well as the rest of us lovely- R & S were going to eat Xmas dinner over there and us girls over to Mae’s but we changed plans and we all ate over to Mary’s and such a dinner. We had a regular one – I’ll let Ruby tell you what she got. Ruby was awfully blue because Sam had to go back.
Margaret has the flu and so far as I can hear is getting along fine. I have to hear thru Mae – She sent her thermometer down by Art. Mae said she would have taken care of Margaret rather than to have her down home at 215 E Dewey but she wasn’t strong yet herself. If Ruby and Lucerne need me I’m willing and ready to go but I thought $30.00 isn’t picked up every week.
Do you hear anything from Martin? Bet he;s anxious to get home. Sure was glad to hear you were all better at home. Ruby, M, and L gave me a flowered petticoat and some handkerchiefs. Think I’ve told you everything Old Santa brought me now. I made Art and the boys a plate of homemade candy and have Mae a pair of Manicure scissors. When did the things arrive home? The girls hadn’t done any shopping to speak of and M and I did most of it Xmas Eve day. The day I went home from Temps.
The baby is getting along fine and Ruby looks well.
Hope to hear from you soon
Love,
Bess
